paras: Today, we are young scientists! We will put different objects into water and observe which ones float and which ones sink. We will also learn about light and heavy objects, discover new describing words, and practise writing simple English sentences.

sections.heading: A. Float or Sink? Look at the objects in the picture. Predict what will happen when each object is placed in a tub of water. Tick (✓) the objects that float and cross (✗) the objects that sink. Then try the experiment with your teacher.

items.a: ✗ Sinks (a typical metal spoon).  Teacher note: paper and feathers may become waterlogged and eventually sink. Children should record what they actually observe during the experiment.

sections.heading: B. Light and Heavy. Answer the following questions.

items.q: Which is heavier: a stone or a feather?
Which is lighter: a pencil or a stone?
Name two objects that usually float in water.
items.a: A leaf and a wooden pencil.

items.q: Name two objects that usually sink in water.
items.a: A stone and a metal spoon.

items.q: Does a heavy object always sink? Discuss with your teacher and give an example.
items.a: No. A large ship is heavy but floats on water.

sections.heading: C1. Learn English with the Picture. Fill in the blanks using the help box.
sections.note: Help box: green, small, wooden, light, heavy.

items.q: A stone is usually ______ compared with a feather.
items.a: A stone is usually heavy compared with a feather.

sections.heading: C2. Write the naming words for any four objects in the picture.

items.a: Pencil  (other correct answers: eraser, feather, spoon)

sections.heading: D1. Think, Observe and Write. Complete the sentences.

items.q: The stone ______ to the bottom of the tub.
items.a: The stone sinks to the bottom of the tub.
The leaf floats on the water.
The feather is light and soft.
The spoon is made of metal.

sections.heading: D2. Write two sentences about your experiment.

items.a: Sample: One object that floated was a wooden pencil.
Sample: One object that sank was a small stone.  (Accept other answers that correctly describe the child's experiment.)
